rules_shown:
The rules of the interaction:
- There are two participants: an Investor and a Trustee.
- Each participant is given 10 dollars to start.
- The Investor chooses an integer amount X, from 0 to 10, to pass to the Trustee.
- Any amount passed is multiplied by 3 on the way, so the Trustee receives 3*X.
- The Trustee then chooses an integer amount Y, from 0 to 3*X, to return.
- Final outcomes: the Investor ends with 10 - X + Y; the Trustee ends with 10 + 3*X - Y.
- This is a single, one-time, anonymous interaction. The participants do not know each other and will not interact again.

reference: Berg, J., Dickhaut, J., & McCabe, K. (1995). Trust, reciprocity, and social history. Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, 25(3), 367-394.
known_results: On average, Investors send about 40-50% of their endowment (e.g., $4 out of $10 initial amount). Trustee returns typically range from 10-20% of what they receive (e.g., return $1.20 from 3*X = $12), though there is significant variability. Positive reciprocation is observed despite the one-time, anonymous interaction.
